author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating to human: workspace-wide filter-param API-shape decision.

Survey of current shapes across extension-client siblings:
- jmap-mail-client (canonical): filter: Option<serde_json::Value>, sort: Option<serde_json::Value> (email_query, mailbox_query, etc.)
- jmap-tasks-client: same as canonical (Option<serde_json::Value>)
- jmap-contacts-client: same as canonical (Option<serde_json::Value>)
- jmap-chat-client: typed Input structs (ChatQueryInput, MessageQueryInput, SpaceQueryInput) with hand-rolled filter construction — diverges from canonical
- jmap-calendars-client: typed bare condition (Option<&CalendarEventFilterCondition>) without compound-filter algebra — third pattern, diverges from canonical

The bead's option A (typed Filter<CalendarEventFilterCondition>) would be a FOURTH pattern. The bead author preferred A as 'matches the workspace's typed-from-day-one stance', but the canonical-template propagation rule (workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates') treats the canonical (mail-client) as authoritative, and the canonical uses Option<serde_json::Value>.

Three coherent paths forward, each is a workspace-level decision:

(a) Bring calendars-client into alignment with canonical: change filter to Option<serde_json::Value>, sort to Option<serde_json::Value>. Same for chat-client (would also need to flatten its typed Inputs). Minimum-divergence path. Stops calendars from being divergent. Does not change typed Input pattern in chat-client.

(b) Bead author's preference: typed Filter<T> wrapper everywhere. Requires reshaping canonical mail-client to Filter<MailFilterCondition> first, then cascading to all 7 siblings. Big workspace-wide sweep but uniform typed-from-day-one shape.

(c) Accept three patterns side-by-side, document the rationale per crate. Each crate's API is internally coherent but the cookie-cutter intent is broken.

The Filter<T> type already exists in jmap-types::query (crate-jmap-types/src/query.rs:104) and supports the compound AND/OR/NOT algebra. The MetadataFilterCondition crate already uses it. So option (b) is technically straightforward — just propagation work.

Per workspace AGENTS.md 'When NOT to file human' rule 3, agent-authored recommendations are excluded from human escalation. The recommendation in the bead body is the bead AUTHOR's (Mark's), with explicit 'Decide before 0.1.x ships widely' contingency. Since the decision impacts canonical mail-client and all 5 other extension-client siblings, escalation is correct.

My recommendation if forced to pick: option (a). The canonical-template rule is a workspace hard rule; deviating in calendars-client only deepens the existing inconsistency. If the workspace wants typed Filter<T>, the bigger sweep (option b) should be a dedicated multi-crate epic that revisits mail-client's API first.

Filed sibling sweep tracker JMAP-ip5u for the if_in_state sweep (separate concern). A similar pattern-decision epic would be needed here once the human picks an option.

Skipping JMAP-1j9k.2 in the /do-beads loop.
